note:
Reviews Mcgrath's book 'Middlemen: Literary Agents and the Making of American Fiction'. The main points are that much of the motivation of literary fiction (as opposed to commercial fiction) revolve around prestige. Most authors and agents make as much or less than their commercial counterparts but the field is much more competitive and selective. The motivation is to produce works of fiction that 'move culture forward' or publish works that are 'unique'.
It also talks about how the first published novella makes or breaks a career, with anonymity/pseudonymity being non-existent and how agents not only look for an interesting work but how to market it based on the authors narrative (youth, history, discovery narrative, etc.).
